Hi Emily — really appreciate the clear asks. We can do a smoothing approach for cohort disbursement; below is a proposed operational and contractual pattern that keeps billing simple and gives startups runway.

Proposal (high level):
- Sandbox Fueling: Allocate an X-credit pool to the cohort and unlock it linearly over 8 weeks (weekly tranche).
- Conversion path: Startups can convert remaining credits into a 6-month prepaid commitment within 90 days of allocation. Conversion results in a pro-rated credit balance and a one-time conversion processing fee (we usually charge 10% of remaining credit value).
- Accounting path: Redwood issues a single invoice for the full voucher face value to Flywheel, with memo lines per cohort. If Flywheel prefers separate invoices per startup, that will need an ops playbook (Marissa can advise).
- Legal: We'll aim for an addendum to the onboarding exhibit that references the voucher schedule rather than amending the MSA.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you confirm the conversion fee and whether we can offer a 0% fee for programs that commit to an enterprise pilot within 6 months?
- Marissa: can you outline the invoicing options and whether we need to set up a dedicated billing code for Flywheel?
- Emily: if that structure looks reasonable, I'll pull together a one-page terms doc and loop in Contracts for a redline.

I've attached a quick draft of proposed voucher terms for your review.

Attachments: [proposed_voucher_terms.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

Thanks, Laura — quick pricing confirmation from my side.

Details:
- Face value: we'll price the cohort voucher pool at the face-value rate (standard self-serve token pricing) unless Flywheel requests a sponsor discount.
- Conversion fee: standard is 10% of remaining credit value; for programs that sign an enterprise pilot (min $20k monthly commit) within 90 days, I can approve a one-time waiver to 5%.
- Early termination / clawback: if a startup is found to abuse usage (spam/abuse or train on regulated PII), we reserve the right to freeze credits and negotiate remediation.
- Volume uplift: if Flywheel bundles vouchers across multiple cohorts (3+), we can tier a 7.5% sponsor discount on face value.

Operational asks:
- We need a clean mapping (CSV) that maps voucher ids to startup emails for redemption and invoicing. Emily, your current schedule looks good — if you can supply a per-startup CSV we can automate issuance.

Attaching a simple pricing matrix so we can align on numbers.

Attachments: [pricing_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

I'll stand by to approve the conversion-fee waiver if Laura confirms the enterprise pilot clause.

— Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Smoothing vouchers for our May cohort / contract checklist

Looping in billing & legal ops notes.

Invoice options:
- Option A (preferred): Single master invoice to Flywheel for the cohort face value. Payment terms NET30. We tag the invoice with a billing code so spend can be broken down to startups internally.
- Option B: Per-startup invoices — doable but will add ~2 business days to onboarding and needs Flywheel to accept many line-items (we can batch them weekly).

Accounting implications: we treat vouchers as prepaid credits for revenue recognition until consumed; we'll need Flywheel to sign the voucher addendum to tie the invoice to an exhibit.

Legal ops: Contracts needs a short addendum and a clause for conversion fees and sponsor discount triggers. Contracts will ask for the CSV mapping and a copy of the cohort schedule. I can shepherd this once we have the draft terms.

If everyone is aligned, I'll kick off an internal ticket with Contracts and Billing and target a redline to Flywheel by EOD Monday.

Marissa Cole
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Voucher addendum redline & DocuSign flow (Flywheel cohort)

Hi Laura / team —

Thanks for the summary. We reviewed the proposed voucher terms and have a few minor edits:

1) Conversion fee clause: suggest explicit formula (conversion fee = 10% x remaining credit USD value) and a carveout that the waiver must be documented in a separate signature page tied to the enterprise pilot contract.
2) Fraud/abuse: add a short remediation pathway (15-day cure period) before credit freeze for edge cases.
3) Invoicing: we need the buyer entity legal name and tax ID for the invoice header and a statement clarifying whether Flywheel will be the payer or if startups may be invoiced directly under Option B.

I'll attach a redline and create a DocuSign envelope once we get the buyer legal details and the CSV mapping. Expect a draft redline (redline_contract.docx) in the next 4 hours.
